newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan rebels said to give ex-governor to Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Afghan rebels said to give ex-governor to Taleban.

text.p: Rebel forces in northern Afghanistan have handed over a captured former provincial governor to the Taleban Islamic movement, a Pakistan-based news service said on Thursday.
It quoted Taleban sources as saying that Ismail Khan, the former governor of the western province of Herat, was transferred on Wednesday night by the forces of General Abdul Malik.
Malik mutinied on Monday against anti-Taleban northern warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
Ismail, who was reported captured by Malik's forces on Monday along with eight of his men, has now been transferred to the Taleban-controlled Herat city, the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) agency said.

Ismail, a trusted lieutenant of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbabi, had fled to Iran after being ousted from Herat by the Taleban in September 1995. But he had been fighting the Taleban in northwest Afghanistan in recent months.
Rabbani's forces forged an alliance with Dostum after being ousted from Kabul by the fundamentalist Taleban militia last September.
